title: Building a Crypto Store on Cloudflare Pages: A Step-by-Step Deployment Guide for Digital Creators
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Stack 01 or Stack 02. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Google Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers. NOWPayments throughout. Deployed in 48 hours. Owned by you.

content.text: In Nigeria, the once-reliable Stripe failed to process payments, leaving digital creators to deal with the uncertainty of restricted commerce infrastructure. The lack of access to platforms like PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle in countries like Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, Cameroon, Tanzania, and the Philippines has left many wondering how to build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free. COREMERCH, a sovereign commerce infrastructure company, offers a solution that bypasses these restrictions and empowers digital creators to sell their products without relying on conventional platforms.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

You can build a digital store that accepts crypto payments using Cloudflare Pages, a platform that offers free hosting and a flexible development environment. By combining Cloudflare Pages with Cloudflare Workers and Supabase, you can create a robust and scalable commerce stack that works even when platforms like Stripe and PayPal fail. This infrastructure is not a workaround, but a base-layer solution that gives you full control over your digital commerce operations.
What You Need Before You Deploy

To deploy a Cloudflare Pages-based digital store, you need a few essential tools: a GitHub account for version control, a Cloudflare account for hosting and Workers, and a NOWPayments account for crypto payment processing. You will also need to set up a Supabase instance for order storage and a Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 account for file delivery. Finally, you will need to choose a cryptocurrency and configure your payment settings in NOWPayments.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Once you have set up your Cloudflare Pages site and configured your payment settings in NOWPayments, it is time to set up your delivery pipeline. This involves creating a Supabase instance to store orders and a Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 account to deliver files. You will also need to configure your Cloudflare Workers to interact with your Supabase instance and NOWPayments account.
You can build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free using Cloudflare Pages and NOWPayments.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

After setting up your payment and delivery pipeline, you are ready to go live and process your first transaction. To do this, you will need to test your site on the mainnet and configure your payment settings to accept crypto payments. Once you have processed your first transaction, you can start selling your products and accepting payments from customers around the world.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start — COREMERCH never owns the code. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. The Cloudflare Workers and Pages deployments are under the customer's Cloudflare account. The Resend account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH has collaborator access during the build period and removes that access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts with no dependency on COREMERCH infrastructure, access, or continued operation.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront: Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages with your product pages and checkout flow pointing to the backend. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires to your backend, confirm the order appears in your database, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link. Only after the complete pipeline test passes should you make the store URL public. COREMERCH runs this complete test before handoff on every deployment.
Cloudflare Pages offers more features and scalability options than GitHub Pages, making it the better choice for serious digital creators.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a Cloudflare Pages-based digital store, follow these steps: Create a GitHub account and set up a Cloudflare account for hosting and Workers. Configure your payment settings in NOWPayments and set up a Supabase instance for order storage. Create a Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 account for file delivery and configure your Cloudflare Workers to interact with your Supabase instance and NOWPayments account. Test your site on the mainnet and configure your payment settings to accept crypto payments.
